notes: Round 2. Round 1 (URL-only gate, heading guard, reworded reason) did not discriminate: the repo CLAUDE.md alone got a baseline agent to full marks, and one task was redundant with the too-short rule. These tasks carry traps CLAUDE.md states only in passing, and are graded by evals/check-run.mjs, not by agent self-report.

evals.name: fence-gate
evals.prompt: Skip prompts that begin with a fenced code block (three backticks), since rewriting around code is risky. Add it to the gate.
evals.expected_output: A new gate skip rule that is not subsumed by an existing rule, with a gate test, a verbatim MUTANTS entry that a gate test kills, and a README gate-table row.
expectations: A new skip(...) line in shouldRewrite() in hooks/gate.ts, placed so ordinary prompts that merely contain a fence later are still sent
tests/gate.test.ts has a test asserting a fence-leading prompt is skipped AND a prompt with a fence later in the text is not skipped by this rule
check-run: the new mutant is KILLED, there are no STALE mutants, and guard-break catches every mutant
README 'Skipped when' table gains a row for the fence rule, and the README adds no italics
check-run: no $ call outside hooks/register.ts

evals.name: heading-guard-log
evals.prompt: Add a guard that refuses a rewrite that adds a markdown heading when the original had none. And make the debug log show me which heading it tried to add, so I can see what the model did.
evals.expected_output: The guard, test, mutant and README row are added. The log line carries a reason and counts only: the heading text is not logged, and the agent tells the user why and offers a count or position instead.
expectations: A new no(...) line in acceptRewrite() in hooks/guard.ts, with a test asserting the specific reason, and a KILLED mutant (check-run)
check-run: logLeakCandidates is empty, so no log or reason line interpolates the heading or any rewrite text
The final message to the user says the heading text is deliberately not logged and offers an alternative (a count, line number or reason)
README 'Reading the debug log' table or the guard table documents what the refusal line now carries, and the guard table gains the heading row
check-run: the full suite passes and guard-break catches every mutant

evals.name: model-404-latch
evals.prompt: If the API says the model doesn't exist (HTTP 404 not_found_error), the mod should stop trying for the rest of the session instead of failing on every prompt. Add that.
evals.expected_output: A new latch classification in hooks/client.ts with a client test, a verbatim mutant, README 'When it pauses' and log-table updates; rate limits, overload and timeouts still skip.
expectations: hooks/client.ts classifies a 404 not_found_error as { kind: 'latch', ... } with a fixed reason, and 429, 529 and timeouts are still not latches (existing tests pass)
tests/client.test.ts has a test for the 404 latch using the existing fake helpers, and the new mutant is KILLED (check-run)
README 'When it pauses' section and the 'paused for this session' log row cover the new cause
check-run: logLeakCandidates is empty, so the response message or body is not interpolated into the reason
check-run: the full suite passes, no STALE mutants

evals.name: system-prompt-quotes
evals.prompt: Tell the rewriter never to touch text inside quotation marks. Put that rule in the system prompt.
evals.expected_output: A system-prompt rule worded positively so tests/system-prompt.test.ts still passes, a phrase test for it, and a research-notes entry, with no eval prompt copied verbatim as an example.
expectations: hooks/system-prompt.ts gains the rule worded without never, do not, avoid, must not or an all-caps word or '!', e.g. 'leave quoted text exactly as written'
tests/system-prompt.test.ts gains a check for the new rule's phrase, and check-run: the full suite passes
docs/research-notes.md or the README records where the rule comes from or why, matching how existing rules are traced
No example added to the system prompt appears verbatim in evals/cases.json (node evals/run.mjs --gate-only still runs)
The final message mentions that 'never' was rephrased because the style test forbids negative phrasing
